figure_candidates.label: Scheme 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Scheme 1. A summarized scheme of paclitaxel biosynthesis. The biosynthesis of paclitaxel from the universal diterpenoid precursor geranylgeranyl
diphosphate (GGPP). Following the committed cyclization to the taxa-4(5),11(12)-diene, multiple oxygenation, acylation and deacetylation reactions, and
oxetane ring formation yield the intermediate baccatin III, to which the functionally important C13-side chain is appended in five additional steps.

figure_candidates.label: Scheme 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Scheme 2. Three proposed mechanistic pathways of oxetane ring forma-
tion. (A) the generally accepted process of oxetane ring formation in
paclitaxel is initiated by the epoxidation of the 4(20)-double bond. (B) (i) A
stepwise, acid-catalysed epoxyester/oxetaneester rearrangement mechanism
(Path A); (ii) a neutral-concerted reaction (Path B); (iii) a dissociative reaction
(Path C).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Proposal of the sequence of oxygenation reactions on the
taxane skeleton based upon the structural investigation of all known 6/8/
6 type taxanes. (A) Early oxygenation steps are proposed to involve C5-, C9-,
C10-, and C13-hydroxylation; C2- and C7-hydroxylation represent intermedi-
ate oxygenation steps; and the formation of the oxetane ring and C9-
carbonyl, as well as C1-hydroxylation, occurs relatively late in the pathway.
The acylation reaction is interspersed between these oxidation reactions.
Finally, the C13-side chain is attached to baccatin III, resulting in the
complete biosynthesis of paclitaxel. (B) Simplified representation of biosyn-
thetic sequences from taxadiene to paclitaxel with coordinates showing the
decoration state. The solid circle colour from dark to light represents the
oxidation sequence from the early stage to the late stage.

figure_candidates.label: Scheme 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Scheme 3. Divergent findings regarding oxetane ring formation in
paclitaxel biosynthesis. (A) Fernie’s group identified a novel epoxidase (a 2-
oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase) could catalyse epoxidation of exo-
taxadiene and endo-taxadiene in combination with T5αH to construct the
oxetane ring, in which the oxetane ring was hypothesized to be
spontaneously generated. (B) Kampranis’s group confirmed that the T5αH
could individually catalyse epoxidation of exo-taxadiene and endo-taxadiene
to form the oxetane ring. (C) A novel cytochrome P450 discovered by Yan’s,
Dai’s and Zhou’s groups could mediate the oxetane ring formation using
compounds 9 and 10 as substrates. (D) Dai’s group confirmed that feeding
substrate 11, a 5-deacetylated derivative of 9, to N. benthamiana leaves
expressing TmCYP1, only the 4β,20-epoxide, 5α-deacetylbaccatin I (11b) was
observed, indicating that the C5-O-acetyl group in substrate is crucial for the
oxetane ring formation but not for the 4(20)-epoxy ring formation.

figure_candidates.label: Scheme 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Scheme 4. Mechanistic insights into oxetane ring formation. (A) Isotopic
labelling experiments. (B) The hexa-ols product (11c) was obtained using
sodium methylate or NH2NH2. (C) The oxetane synthase (TmCYP1, TOT1 and
CYP725A55) was not able to transform 9b/10b to 9a/10a in N. benthamiana
transient expression or insect cells system. (D) Proposed formation
mechanism of oxetane ring based on DFT calculations. (i) Yan’s group and
Lei’s group obtained a more stable oxonium ion intermediate (int 1), which
can produce epoxide ring product and oxetane product, the two products
require involvement of C5-acetoxy; (ii) Dai’s group and Zhou’s group
obtained a cationic intermediate FeIII� O� C� C+ (N1), which can also form
epoxide and oxetane product. In this process, the C5-O-acetyl group in
substrate is crucial for the oxetane ring formation but not for the 4(20)-
epoxy ring formation by oxetanase, which is a cascade oxidation-concerted
acyl rearrangement mechanism of oxetane ring formation.
